title: Rust engine: closing the switch-over gaps
summary: research/SWITCHOVER.md (#270) audited every JavaScript game file due for deletion and listed 14 gaps that block switching play.html to the Rust engine. Most are now merged: diagnostics, vehicle texture alpha, iPhone audio and sound mode, multiplayer links and context-loss recovery, train, rain and crash sounds, shadows and prefetch, and the Single Race setup and Rider Gear menus. The page shell (#279) and the main-menu Jukebox (#282) are open pull requests, not shipped. All checks were host Chromium and WebKit on a Mac; nothing was run on a real phone.
details: Merged: #271 F3 diagnostics overlay (Off / Performance / Debug, also ?debug=1 and ?debug=2). #272 vehicle and rider texture alpha: the original materials all enable alpha blending, so bike sprockets, spoked wheels, quad shocks and frames had drawn as black squares in both the JavaScript and Rust builds; they now cut out correctly. #273 documented that the Arlington (ENV08) train is the original's single-detail geometry (locomotive 451 triangles); no higher-detail mesh exists to restore. #274 and #275: the multiplayer train test is stable again (the failure was deck-placement timing, not a Rust difference), and the lobby page lists riders once connected.

Merged: #276 iPhone silent switch (navigator.audioSession playback or ambient, a Settings > Extras row), the saved Sound mode applied at ride start (Enhanced by default), race intro skip by tap, click or pad, and the Fullscreen row hidden where unsupported. #277 train and rain sounds and the Crazy/Gorn crash boom, with equal sound counts in the JavaScript and Rust engines (ENV08 train 11, ENV04 rain 1, ENV03 boom 1), a Settings > Audio song picker, and a fallback to the original audio when the music stream is missing. #278 multiplayer links open the lobby forms and host or join with play=1, invite links carry the rider's own ATV, race links keep cheats=, motorcycle race links start, and a lost WebGL context shows 'Restoring graphics...' and reopens the ride. Difference from the JavaScript build: a single-player ride restarts after context loss, where the JavaScript build rebuilt in place.

Merged: #280 CPU and remote-rider shadows and parallel ride prefetch (env01 load 4.6-5.2 s against 5.8-6.4 s before, at 150 ms simulated latency). #281 the Single Race setup page (tabs, laps, CPU riders, difficulty, Start Race), Rider Gear editing with dressed previews (pictured), controller pinning, non-standard pad glyphs and the flip-arm buzz. Not merged yet: #279 page shell (install banner and iOS help, offline use with the service worker precaching engine.html and the wasm, the five analytics events, and render scale that steps 1.5x to 1.25 to 1.0 on slow frames, observed 1.5 > 1.25 > 1.0 under a 20x CPU throttle) and #282 main-menu Jukebox (the soundtrack player shared by menus and rides). Both are open pull requests and are described here as built, not shipped.
Next: a draft switch-over pull request (play.html to the Rust engine, JavaScript game deleted) is being prepared. The owner decides when to switch after phone testing.
limitation: All measurements and screenshots are from host Chromium and WebKit on a Mac; none are physical-phone results, and the load-time, throttle and render-scale numbers do not predict phone performance. iPhone silent switch behaviour, install and offline flows, and haptic buzz still need a real device. #279 and #282 are open and unmerged. The Rust engine is not yet the default play.html; the JavaScript game remains until the owner switches after phone testing.
